translation_en: ‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Sulayman al-Raba‘i narrated to us: Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji narrated to us, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Gold for gold, like for like.” Then he mentioned a report like it.

Abu al-Tahir, Harun ibn Sa‘id al-Ayli, and Ahmad ibn ‘Isa narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Makhramah informed me, from his father, who said: I heard Sulayman ibn Yasar say that he heard Malik ibn Abi ‘Amir narrating from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not sell one dinar for two dinars, or one dirham for two dirhams.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: I came asking who would exchange dirhams. Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, who was with ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, said, “Show us your gold, then come to us when our servant arrives, and we will give you your silver.” ‘Umar said, “No, by Allah, you must give him his silver or return his gold, for the Messenger of Allah said: ‘Silver for gold is usury unless exchanged hand to hand; wheat for wheat is usury unless exchanged hand to hand; barley for barley is usury unless exchanged hand to hand; and dates for dates are usury unless exchanged hand to hand.’”
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq narrated to us, from Ibn ‘Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, with this chain.

‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, who said: I was in Syria in a gathering that included Muslim ibn Yasar. Abu al-Ash‘ath came and sat down. I asked him to narrate to our companion the hadith of ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit. He said: We went on an expedition under Mu‘awiyah and gained much booty, including silver vessels. Mu‘awiyah ordered a man to sell them in exchange for people’s stipends, and people rushed to do so. When ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit heard, he stood and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah forbid selling gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, except equal for equal, item for item. Whoever gives or takes more has engaged in usury. People returned what they had taken. When Mu‘awiyah heard, he delivered a speech and said, “What is the matter with men who report hadiths from the Messenger of Allah that we, who were with him, never heard?” ‘Ubadah stood and repeated the story, then said: “We will report what we heard from the Messenger of Allah, even if Mu‘awiyah dislikes it—or is angered by it. I do not care if I do not accompany him in his army for a dark night.” Hammad said: This or something like it.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi ‘Umar both reported from ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, from Ayyub, with this chain and a report like it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Amr al-Naqid, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah’s. Ishaq said: He informed us; the other two said: Waki‘ narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash‘ath, from ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, like for like, equal for equal, hand to hand. When these kinds differ, sell as you wish, provided it is hand to hand.”

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ and Wasil ibn ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Zur‘ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Dates for dates, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, and salt for salt, like for like, hand to hand. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in usury, except when the kinds differ.”
Abu Sa‘id al-Ashajj narrated it to me: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, with this chain, but he did not mention “hand to hand.”

Abu Kurayb and Wasil ibn ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nu‘m, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Gold for gold, weight for weight, like for like; silver for silver, weight for weight, like for like. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in usury.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah al-Qa‘nabi narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi Tamim, from Sa‘id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “A dinar for a dinar, with no difference between them; a dirham for a dirham, with no difference between them.”
Abu al-Tahir narrated it to me: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: I heard Malik ibn Anas say that Musa ibn Abi Tamim narrated to me, with this chain and a report like it.

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Abu al-Minhal, who said: A partner of mine sold silver on credit until the season or pilgrimage, then came and told me. I said, “This is not sound.” He said, “I sold it in the market, and no one objected.” I went to al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib and asked him. He said: The Prophet came to Madinah while we were making this sale and said: “Whatever is hand to hand is permissible; whatever is deferred is usury.” He said: Go to Zayd ibn Arqam, for he is a greater merchant than I. I went to him and asked, and he said the same.

‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh al-‘Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Habib, who heard Abu al-Minhal say: I asked al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib about currency exchange. He said, “Ask Zayd ibn Arqam, for he knows better.” I asked Zayd, and he said, “Ask al-Bara’, for he knows better.” Then both said: The Messenger of Allah forbade selling silver for gold on credit.

Abu al-Rabi‘ al-‘Ataki narrated to us: ‘Abbad ibn al-‘Awwam narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq informed us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade exchanging silver for silver and gold for gold except equally, and ordered us to buy silver for gold as we wished and gold for silver as we wished. A man asked him, “Hand to hand?” He said, “That is how I heard it.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed me: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us: Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from Yahya, Ibn Abi Kathir, from Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq, that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah informed him that Abu Bakrah said the Messenger of Allah forbade us in a report like it.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sarh informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani informed me that he heard ‘Ulayy ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi say: I heard Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd al-Ansari say: A necklace containing beads and gold was brought to the Messenger of Allah while he was at Khaybar. It was from the spoils and was being sold. The Messenger ordered that the gold in it be removed separately, then said: “Gold for gold, weight for weight.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Abu Shuja‘ Sa‘id ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Abi ‘Imran, from Hanish al-San‘ani, from Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd, who said: On the day of Khaybar I bought a necklace for twelve dinars containing gold and beads. I separated it and found more than twelve dinars’ worth of gold. I mentioned this to the Prophet, who said: “It must not be sold until it is separated.”
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn Yazid, with this chain and a report like it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Ja‘far, from al-Jullah Abu Kathir, who narrated to me: Hanish al-San‘ani narrated to me, from Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah on the day of Khaybar, trading a measure of gold for two or three dinars. The Messenger of Allah said: “Do not sell gold for gold except weight for weight.”

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Qurrah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Ma‘afiri, ‘Amr ibn al-Harith, and others, that ‘Amir ibn Yahya al-Ma‘afiri informed them, from Hanish, who said: We were with Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd on a military expedition, and I acquired a necklace containing gold, silver, and jewels. I wanted to buy it, so I asked Fadalah. He said: “Remove its gold and place it on one side of the scale, and put your gold on the other. Take no more than an equal amount, for I heard the Messenger of Allah say: ‘Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day must take no more than an equal amount.’”

Harun ibn Ma‘ruf narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us: ‘Amr informed me; and Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from ‘Amr ibn al-Harith, that Abu al-Nadr told him that Busr ibn Sa‘id told him, from Ma‘mar ibn ‘Abd Allah: He sent his servant with a measure of wheat and said, “Sell it, then buy barley with its price.” The servant went and took a measure and some extra. When he returned and told Ma‘mar, Ma‘mar said, “Why did you do that? Go back and return it, and take only an equal amount, for I heard the Messenger of Allah say: ‘Food for food, like for like.’” Their food at that time was barley. He was asked, “But they are not the same kind.” He said, “I fear it may resemble it.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa‘nab narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, who heard Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab narrate that Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa‘id told him: The Messenger of Allah appointed a man from the Ansar of Banu ‘Adi over Khaybar. He returned with fine dates. The Messenger asked, “Are all the dates of Khaybar like this?” He said, “No, by Allah, Messenger of Allah. We buy one measure for two measures of mixed dates.” The Messenger said: “Do not do that. Either exchange like for like, or sell these and use their price to buy those. The same applies to weighing.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from ‘Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah appointed a man over Khaybar. He came to him with fine dates. The Messenger asked whether all Khaybar’s dates were like that. He said, “No, by Allah, Messenger of Allah. We take one measure of these for two measures, or two for three.” The Messenger said: “Do not do that. Sell the mixed dates for dirhams, then buy fine dates with the dirhams.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed us: Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhazi narrated to us: Mu‘awiyah narrated to us; and Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi and ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me—and their wording is used—Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us: Mu‘awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us: Yahya, Ibn Abi Kathir, narrated to me: I heard ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Abd al-Ghafir say: I heard Abu Sa‘id say: Bilal brought some barni dates. The Messenger asked, “Where did these come from?” Bilal said, “We had poor dates, so I exchanged two measures of them for one measure to serve the Prophet.” The Messenger said: “Ah! That is the essence of usury. Do not do that. If you want to buy dates, sell them in another transaction, then buy with the price.” Ibn Sahl’s report does not mention “then.”

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn A‘yan narrated to us: Ma‘qil narrated to us, from Abu Qaza‘ah al-Bahili, from Abu Nadhrah, from Abu Sa‘id, who said: Dates were brought to the Messenger of Allah. He said, “These are not like our dates.” The man said, “Messenger of Allah, we exchanged two measures of our dates for one measure of these.” The Messenger said: “This is usury. Return them, then sell your dates and buy these for us.”

‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Sa‘id al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadhrah, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas about currency exchange. He said, “Is it hand to hand?” I said yes, and he said, “Then there is no harm.” I told Abu Sa‘id and said Ibn ‘Abbas permitted it when it was hand to hand. He said, “Did he say that? We will write to him so he does not give you that ruling.” By Allah, a young man of the Messenger of Allah brought him dates, and he objected, saying, “It seems these are not from the dates of our land.” The man said: “There was something lacking in this year’s dates, so I took these and added some extra.” The Messenger said: “You have multiplied it and engaged in usury. Do not approach this. If something about your dates troubles you, sell them, then buy the dates you want.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Abd al-A‘la informed us: Dawud informed us, from Abu Nadhrah, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbas about currency exchange, and they saw no harm in it. I was sitting with Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri and asked him. He said, “Any excess is usury.” I objected because of what they had said. He replied, “I will only tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah.” A man who owned date palms brought him a measure of good dates, while the Prophet’s dates were of another kind. The Prophet asked, “Where did you get this?” He said, “I took two measures and bought this one measure, because the market price of this is such-and-such and of that is such-and-such.” The Messenger said: “Woe to you! You have engaged in usury. If you want to do that, sell your dates for another commodity, then buy whichever dates you wish with that commodity.” Abu Sa‘id said: “Is date for date more deserving of being usury, or silver for silver?” He later went to Ibn ‘Umar, who forbade it; he did not go to Ibn ‘Abbas. Abu al-Sahba’ told me that he asked Ibn ‘Abbas about it in Makkah, and Ibn ‘Abbas disliked it.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Shayban, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Sa‘id, who said: In the Messenger of Allah’s time we were given mixed dates. We used to sell two measures for one. The Messenger heard of this and said: “No two measures of dates for one measure, no two measures of wheat for one, and no one dirham for two.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad, Muhammad ibn Hatim, and Ibn Abi ‘Umar all reported from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah—and the wording is Ibn ‘Abbad’s. Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Abu Salih, who said: I heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri say: “A dinar for a dinar and a dirham for a dirham, like for like. Whoever gives or takes more has engaged in usury.” I said to him, “Ibn ‘Abbas says otherwise.” He said: “I met Ibn ‘Abbas and asked whether what he says is something he heard from the Messenger of Allah or found in Allah’s Book, Mighty and Sublime. He said, ‘I did not hear it from the Messenger of Allah or find it in Allah’s Book, but Usamah ibn Zayd told me that the Prophet said: Usury is in deferred exchange.’”
